t: You're at Lancaster Gate, a mid-19th century development in Bayswater, just north of Kensington Gardens. A few notable people have a connection to the area. James Sant, the Victorian painter, lived here. He was known for portraits of aristocratic women and children, and he was appointed Principal Court Painter in Ordinary to Queen Victoria. Neville Elliott-Cooper, who went on to receive the Victoria Cross, the highest award for gallantry, was born here. So was Henry Herbert, the 7th Earl of Carnarvon, who later served as racing manager to Queen Elizabeth the Second.
